correctness.rationale: For each mode finite second moment and \(a_i^2+s_i<1\) ensure uniform \(L^2\) convergence of both product sums. Independent-depth centered first-factor recursions give \(\operatorname{Var}(S_+)=s/[(1-a)^2(B-s)]\), \(\operatorname{Var}(S_-)=\tau^2s/[(1-a)^2(B-\tau^2s)]\), and \(\operatorname{Cov}(S_+,S_-)=-\tau s/[(1-a)^2(B+\tau s)]\). Their half-sum gives the claimed exact risk; arbitrary across-coordinate noise dependence disappears from squared Euclidean risk. Derivatives prove global strict convexity and opposing endpoint signs. The scalar optimizer quartic is equivalent to positive-denominator first-order conditions, and the golden limit and risk ratios follow by continuous root convergence. Uniform \(L^2\) tails prove finite-depth minimizer convergence. A standalone Python rational verifier passed 109 cases, including a nonsymmetric centered noise law and correlated diagonal modes. No finite experiment is used as proof of generality.

value.rationale: Mirror strength is a genuine free parameter of a recently proposed stochastic inverse-Hessian estimator, not an arbitrary slice. The theorem establishes a structurally nontrivial and universally interior variance optimum contrary to the full-reflection skewness objective; yields explicit implementable scalar calibration, a sharp algebraic noise-boundary constant, and a robust commuting-matrix convex tuning rule. It connects to finite-depth risk through uniform convergence and supplies a concrete roughly 20.5 percent paired-variance improvement. It does not falsely claim benefit for scalar inversion when the Hessian is exactly known or general end-to-end training.
